STALE -- fixed since filing. All eight wrappers now take an AiaFetcher parameter.

The bead says the wrappers "bake &NoAiaFetcher internally (lines 770, 855, 932, 1001, 1034, 1085, 1155, 1288)" and that the only way to wire a fetcher in is to abandon the wrapper for verify_chain. Checked each of the eight named: verify_tls_server, verify_tls_client_dns, verify_tls_client_mailbox, verify_smime_signer, verify_smime_recipient, verify_code_signer, verify_time_stamper and verify_ocsp_responder all declare `aia: &A` and are generic over A: AiaFetcher. A deployer wanting AIA reassembly for TLS server validation passes their fetcher and keeps the identity binding and post-validation EKU/KU glue the bead was worried about reimplementing.

Independently corroborated while fixing q9hv.17: those same five wrapper examples in pkix-chain/README.md had to gain explicit &NoAiaFetcher (and &DefaultVerifier) arguments precisely because the parameters exist -- the README was stale against the signatures, which is the mirror image of this bead being stale against them.

The remaining &NoAiaFetcher occurrences are all deliberate and none is a wrapper:
- lib.rs:486 inside verify_chain_default, the intentionally-minimal entry point that also fixes DefaultVerifier
- lib.rs:635 inside Verifier::new_no_aia, which says so in its name
- lib.rs:33 and :1349, rustdoc examples showing a caller passing it explicitly

So there is an opt-in path, and the no-AIA choices that remain are named rather than silent.
